templates_considered: SEC-013 requests_have_timeout: fits the timeout part. Its rule uses statement.param_bound, which judges an omitted timeout at its 10s default and so passes it; added statement.param_required to require an explicit value
LOG-010 external_calls_handle_errors: fits the error-handling part. Its rule lists only api.request; its own limits note says to add the other external statements, so I extended it
AUTH-010, DATA-010, VND-001, SEC-012, SEC-011: considered for neighbouring concerns; not part of the ask (SEC-012 noted in reply as a finding, not written)
Recipes: none fit; no recipe covers resilience of external calls

rules.covers: every external request has a timeout of 30s or less
every external request sets its timeout explicitly, so an omitted one is not silently judged at the default
every external call sits in a try block so a vendor failure reaches error handling

ask_parts_not_covered.part: the catch block actually handles the failure (fallback, error to caller)
timeouts on ai.external.mcp.*, db.external.*.direct_query and ai.agent.run
ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists; these statements take no timeout param

ask_parts_not_covered.part: error handling is good in practice, not just present

assumptions: 'any external API call' includes ai.agent.run (model provider call) and external DB direct queries, so I included them in LOG-010 but they have no timeout rule
util.send_email was not treated as an external API call
a 30-second max is the template's value and a reasonable one for this customer; I did not confirm it with the customer
statement.param_required treats an explicit timeout = 10 as not set (the catalogue says the pull drops it); this edge case is not handled
the timeout in acme_get_tracking (60) should be flagged; I did not evaluate, only read it
workspace_names_used: shipfast (api.shipfast.example) vendor calls in acme_get_tracking, acme_sync_shipping_rates, api/app/shipments/quote
confusions: SEC-013 template rule uses statement.param_bound alone; its description says an omitted timeout is judged at 10s, so the rule can pass a call with no timeout. The template summary says 'times out within 30 seconds' and doesn't mention that the timeout must be set; I had to infer that statement.param_required was the missing piece
statement.param_required's description excludes a value equal to the default (timeout = 10) because a pull drops it. Not clear if an explicit timeout = 10 is reported or silently passes
LOG-010's template limits note says to add other external statements, but the template's rule and the 'Where values go' section differ on whether api.request alone is enough; I extended it

statement.containment: the catalogue says try_catch means the try branch, and that a try_catch.try name is accepted; the template used plain try_catch. I used try_catch.try to be explicit, unverified whether it differs
xano policy parse human-readable output drops the severity line, while -o json keeps it; easy to misread the file as lacking severity
ai.agent.run is not in the templates' external-call list; its inclusion is my judgement
wished_for: a template or recipe for 'external calls are resilient': timeout set explicitly and bounded, call inside try, retry bounded
a note on the SEC-013 template saying the timeout must be explicit, or a second rule shipped with the template
a check that confirms the catch branch does something (not just exists)
a check that bounds while-loops that contain external calls
a worked example combining statement.param_required and statement.param_bound on timeout
why_confidence: The timeout half is covered by an explicit-set rule plus a max-bound rule, so an omitted timeout is caught. The error-handling half only proves the call is in a try block, not that the failure is handled, and the timeout bound cannot cover AI or external-DB statements. Neither policy was evaluated against the workspace, so the flagged list in the reply is from reading, not from the platform.
